strengths: Practical significance and efficiency: The paper targets a meaningful bottleneck in diffusion-based super-resolution. While recent 1-step methods rely on multi-billion parameter text-to-image (T2I) backbones (e.g., OSEDiff, AddSR) with high GPU memory demands and tendencies to hallucinate unfaithful details, RSD operates on a compact 174M parameter architecture, achieving 0.059s inference with substantially lower VRAM usage (~539 MB).

Solid theoretical motivation: Proposition 3.1 provides an exact tractable formulation for distilling ResShift by introducing an auxiliary 'fake' ResShift model, avoiding heuristic truncations previously employed in score identity distillation frameworks and rigorously bridging trajectory KL minimization with conditional bridge distillation.

Extensive empirical evaluation: The method is comprehensively evaluated across both real-world and synthetic datasets (RealSR, RealSet65, DRealSR, ImageNet-Test, DIV2K) across two different evaluation protocols (SinSR and OSEDiff benchmarks), convincingly demonstrating strong fidelity (PSNR/SSIM) alongside competitive perceptual metrics (CLIPIQA, MUSIQ, LPIPS).

Thorough ablation studies: The authors cleanly isolate the benefits of multistep training trajectories during student optimization and analyze the specific impacts of supervised LPIPS and GAN losses on the perception-distortion trade-off.
weaknesses: Conceptual overlap with prior distillation techniques: The core distillation strategy—training an auxiliary 'fake' network on student outputs to match teacher predictions, accompanied by a GAN loss on network features—closely parallels established paradigms in the generative literature, notably DMD2 (Yin et al., 2024), SiD (Zhou et al., 2024), and IBMD (Gushchin et al., 2025). The conceptual novelty lies mainly in applying and adapting these principles to the ResShift/diffusion bridge SR setting.

Heavy reliance on supervised/GAN objectives for peak performance: As demonstrated in Table 6 and the 'distill only' rows of Tables 1 and 2, pure distillation yields relatively modest improvements; the substantial gains in perceptual metrics and sharpness largely stem from the standard supervised LPIPS and DMD2-style GAN losses.

Absence of human perceptual user study: Considering that no-reference image quality assessment metrics (e.g., MUSIQ, CLIPIQA, NIQE) can be biased or sensitive to adversarial sharpening, a formalized user study (Mean Opinion Score / pairwise preference) would provide more definitive evidence of perceptual superiority over SinSR and OSEDiff.

Minor typographic and drafting errors: Several typos are present in the text (e.g., 'paroblem' on page 5, 'aulixiary' on page 16, and redundant phrases in Appendix A.1) that slightly detract from the presentation quality.

strengths: Practical motivation and strong efficiency-quality trade-off: The paper addresses the severe computational cost and hallucination issues of text-to-image (T2I) based SR models (e.g., SUPIR, OSEDiff with 1.7B-4.8B parameters) and the blurriness of prior 1-step distilled models (SinSR). RSD operates with only 174M parameters and ~540 MB inference memory, achieving 1-step inference while matching or exceeding the perceptual quality of large models.

Theoretical formulation and principled derivation: Proposition 3.1 provides a tractable minimax formulation to avoid backpropagating through the fake model re-training loop. The appendix clearly explains how RSD optimizes the KL divergence between joint trajectory distributions across all timesteps, contrasting with VSD and SDS which optimize marginal distributions.

Extensive experimental validation: The method is thoroughly evaluated across standard synthetic and real-world benchmarks (RealSR, RealSet65, DRealSR, ImageNet-Test, DIV2K) using both full-reference fidelity metrics (PSNR, SSIM) and perceptual/no-reference metrics (LPIPS, CLIPIQA, MUSIQ, DISTS, NIQE, MANIQA).

Training efficiency over existing baselines: Because RSD is simulation-free (evaluating the teacher score directly rather than unrolling all reverse trajectory steps during training as in SinSR), it converges approximately 3 times faster in training wall-clock time.

Insightful ablation studies: Clear ablations justify the number of training timesteps N, the impact of multistep training versus single-step training, and the distinct contributions of the supervised LPIPS and GAN losses.
weaknesses: Conceptual novelty is largely incremental over existing distillation paradigms: While adapting the objective to ResShift is well executed, the core formulation (training an auxiliary 'fake' denoiser to match a teacher) is heavily inspired by existing distribution matching works such as SiD, DMD2, FGM, and especially conditional Inverse Bridge Matching Distillation (IBMD). The addition of discriminator and LPIPS losses mirrors established pipelines (e.g., DMD2, OSEDiff).

Perceptual headroom compared to large T2I priors: In scenarios requiring rich semantic prior hallucination (e.g., generating fine text, complex high-frequency natural foliage), large T2I-based methods like SUPIR/OSEDiff still demonstrate superior visual detail and no-reference scores (e.g., Table 3 and Figure 6).

Minor presentation and typographical issues: A few typos are present in the text, such as 'paroblem' on page 5 and slight inconsistencies in notation in Proposition 3.1 and Appendix I (e.g., sign conventions in Eq. 35 vs Eq. 8) that require careful reading to reconcile.

strengths: Practical efficiency and low latency: By distilling the 15-step ResShift model into a 1-step generator, the proposed RSD maintains a compact architecture (174M parameters, ~540MB inference GPU memory, ~0.06s latency on an A100), avoiding the prohibitive memory and compute footprints of billion-parameter text-to-image (T2I) baselines such as SUPIR and OSEDiff.

Improved training throughput over SinSR: RSD is simulation-free during distillation and does not require unrolling the full multi-step reverse trajectory of the ResShift teacher at each iteration, resulting in approximately 3x faster training convergence compared to SinSR.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The paper conducts extensive benchmarks across diverse synthetic and real-world datasets (RealSR, RealSet65, DRealSR, ImageNet-Test, DIV2K-Val) under multiple standard evaluation protocols and metrics.
weaknesses: Limited methodological and theoretical originality: The core concept of using an auxiliary 'fake' model to bypass backpropagating through the data-dependent score/expectation is heavily derived from prior diffusion distillation frameworks, notably Score Identity Distillation (SiD), DMD/DMD2, Flow Generator Matching (FGM), and Inverse Bridge Matching Distillation (IBMD). Proposition 3.1 is essentially an application of the standard dual/minimax expectation formulation to the discrete ResShift setting rather than a fundamentally new theoretical insight.

Heavily reliant on auxiliary supervised and adversarial losses: As demonstrated in Table 6 and the 'distill only' rows in Tables 1 and 2, removing the supervised LPIPS and GAN losses causes substantial performance drops (e.g., LPIPS worsens from 0.2726 to 0.3552 on RealSR). This indicates that the perceptual advantages over SinSR are largely driven by the combination of external supervised losses (LPIPS + DMD2-style discriminator) rather than the distillation objective alone.

Perceptual ceiling relative to large T2I priors: While RSD achieves better fidelity (PSNR/SSIM) and much lower computational cost than T2I-based models, its perceptual reconstruction capability remains strictly bounded by the compact ResShift teacher and ImageNet pre-training, struggling to synthesize plausible fine textures and structural details in challenging real-world scenes compared to models with web-scale priors.

Minor inconsistencies and notation typos in the appendix derivations: In the proof of Proposition 3.1 (Equations 35 and 36), there are confusing typographical errors regarding signs and inner products (e.g., writing $2\langle f_\phi(x_t, y_0, t) + f^*(x_t, y_0, t), \hat{x}_0 \rangle$ under the bracket labeled 'does not depend on $\phi$'), which detracts from the mathematical rigor.
